A C# PascalCase property binds to the camelCase YAML key. Dictionary keys are never renamed by the convention. Enum-like string values are parsed case-insensitively; some (like load.mode) additionally strip - and _ before matching, confirmed per-case in the file-flow census (docs/reference/flow/keys.json), not assumed for these new document kinds.

Blank entries are dropped, each remaining entry is trimmed and stripped of a single surrounding bracket pair (SplitQualifiedName, so [raw] equals raw), and duplicates are removed case-insensitively with the first spelling kept (NormalizeSchemas, src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.cs:176-197). keys.description: One schema name to skip, matched case-insensitively against the object's schema (and, for the Schema category, against the schema's own name, so excluding a schema also keeps its CREATE SCHEMA out of the snapshot). An object that belongs to no schema (a database DDL trigger) is never excluded this way. System schemas are already excluded from the Schema category regardless of this list (dbo, sys, INFORMATION_SCHEMA, guest, and the fixed database roles), so naming one here only affects that schema's objects.

How many connections script objects at the same time. Maps to SourceControlScripting.Parallelism (src/SqlFlow.Core/SourceControl/SourceControlFlow.cs:120-124) and is handed to the scripter's connection pool (SmoDatabaseScripter.ScripterPool, src/SqlFlow.SourceControl/SmoDatabaseScripter.cs:80). It exists because scripting one object with full DRI, indexes, triggers, and extended properties costs SMO dozens of small round trips: the cost is round-trip latency, not server work, so against a remote instance a single table takes about a second of wall-clock while the server sits idle, and a few hundred objects walked on one connection take many minutes with the trace apparently frozen. Each lane is an independent connection with its own SMO Server and Scripter (SmoDatabaseScripter.ScriptingLane) because SMO objects are not thread-safe, though separate instances on separate connections are; enumeration stays on the single lead connection and each lane scripts by Urn, which resolves against whichever server it is handed. The snapshot is therefore byte-identical whatever this is set to (objects are re-sorted by relative path and warnings ordinally, so nothing depends on which lane finished first) and only the wall-clock and the connection count on the scripted server change. A category with fewer objects than lanes uses only as many lanes as it has objects, and a lane opens its connection on the first object it is handed, so a narrow scripting.include never opens connections it does not use. Lanes are reused across categories, so a snapshot pays the connect cost once per lane rather than once per category. Set it to 1 to walk the database on a single connection.

Required descriptor of the SQL Server database to script: exactly one of source.server (a name declared under connections:) or source.connection (an inline reference, which synthesizes a connection named 'source'), plus optional source.provider and source.database. Binds to the private SourceControlSourceYaml and is consumed only inside YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.Map (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.cs:76-81); there is no separate public model type for it, its fields land directly on SourceControlFlow.Server/Database (src/SqlFlow.Core/SourceControl/SourceControlFlow.cs:21-30).

keys.description: An inline connection string or a ${env:...}/${keyvault:...} reference for the database to script, used when the connection is not already declared under connections:. ResolveEndpointConnection (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:112-154) registers it as a new connection under the fixed synthetic name 'source' (YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.SourceConnectionName, src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.cs:32, used at line 78), so the flow addresses it as '@source' (SourceControlFlow.ConnectionReference, src/SqlFlow.Core/SourceControl/SourceControlFlow.cs:24-26) exactly as if it had been declared 'connections: { source: <value> }'. The trimmed value is resolved at run time by SourceControlService through the same ISecretResolver every connection reference goes through (src/SqlFlow.SourceControl/SourceControlService.cs:49-51); a literal that looks like it embeds a credential (password=, pwd=, secret=, etc.) only produces a non-fatal validate/run warning (SecretHygiene), unlike repository.username/repository.secret it is never rejected at parse time for being a literal.

(src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:121-122). Neither set: "{source}: 'source' needs a connection. Set 'source.connection' to a connection string or a ${...} reference, or 'source.server' to a name declared under 'connections:'." (YamlDocumentParts.cs:139-141). If connections: already declares an entry named 'source': "{source}: 'source.connection' is set, but 'connections:' already declares 'source'. Either rename that connection or use 'source.server: source'." (YamlDocumentParts.cs:146-148). The resulting synthesized connection is still subject to RequireSqlServerConnection (see source.server).

keys.default: null (the connection's default catalog, resolved at run time)
keys.description: The database to script; maps to SourceControlFlow.Database (src/SqlFlow.Core/SourceControl/SourceControlFlow.cs:28-30). Blank/whitespace normalizes to null (YamlDocumentParts.NullIfBlank, src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.cs:93). When null, SmoDatabaseScripter.Script resolves the database from the connection string's 'Initial Catalog' if present, else the opened ServerConnection's own database name (src/SqlFlow.SourceControl/SmoDatabaseScripter.cs:91-96). Scripted objects land under a folder named for whichever database name is resolved (SmoDatabaseScripter.cs:221-225; src/SqlFlow.SourceControl/SnapshotWriter.cs:32-33), so one repository can hold side-by-side snapshots of several databases as long as each scm flow's PathScope (the resolved database name) differs (src/SqlFlow.SourceControl/SourceControlService.cs:65).

(src/SqlFlow.SourceControl/SmoDatabaseScripter.cs:95-96). A named database the login cannot reach: SqlFlowException "Database '<name>' was not found on the server, or the login cannot access it." (SmoDatabaseScripter.cs:98-100).

keys.appliesWhen: source.connection is set (ignored entirely when source.server is used instead - this key is then simply never read)
keys.description: The provider of an inline source.connection, parsed by the same ParseProvider used for connections.<name>.provider (see that entry for the exact matching rules and accepted synonyms, e.g. 'sqlserver' for 'mssql'). In practice this must resolve to mssql or azdb: whatever it produces, the connection ends up subject to the same RequireSqlServerConnection guard as source.server, so authoring 'mysql'/'postgres'/'oracle' here parses fine but the flow still fails immediately afterward for not being SQL Server.

keys.appliesWhen: source.connection is not set (exactly one of source.server or source.connection is required)
keys.description: The name of a connection declared under connections: to use as the database to script; resolved by ResolveEndpointConnection (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:112-154) into SourceControlFlow.Server (src/SqlFlow.Core/SourceControl/SourceControlFlow.cs:21-22), which the flow then addresses as '@<server>' via the computed ConnectionReference property (SourceControlFlow.cs:24-26) when SourceControlService resolves it with ConnectionRole.Source (src/SqlFlow.SourceControl/SourceControlService.cs:49-51). SMO scripts SQL Server only, so whichever connection this (or a synthesized source.connection) resolves to must come back MSSQL or AZDB; a foreign provider (mysql/postgres/oracle) is rejected at parse time via RequireSqlServerConnection rather than failing deep inside a run (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.cs:81).

(src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:130-131). Once resolved (via either source.server or source.connection), a non-SQL-Server connection: FlowValidationException "{source}: the source connection '<name>' is '<kind>'; a source-control flow's source must be SQL Server (mssql or azdb)." where <kind> is one of MSSQL, AZDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle (RequireSqlServerConnection, src/SqlFlow.Yaml/YamlDocumentParts.cs:168-177, called at YamlSourceControlFlowLoader.cs:81).
